thread.title: Dollar mixed ahead of jobs report, Powell remarks - MarketWatch

author: William Watts
title: Dollar mixed ahead of jobs report, Powell remarks - MarketWatch
text:
The U.S. dollar rallied versus major rivals Friday morning after a much stronger-than-expected rise in December nonfarm payrolls sparked a jump in Treasury yields and called into question whether the Federal Reserve will slow the pace of interest-rate hikes.
The moves come ahead of eagerly anticipated remarks by Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell and as investor appetite for assets perceived as risky got a lift after the People’s Bank of China cut its reserve requirements.
Read: Stressed-out stock traders face Friday hurdles posed by jobs report, Fed’s Powell
The U.S. added 312,000 new jobs in December , far exceeding the consensus forecast of 182,000 produced by a MarketWatch survey of economists. The unemployment rate rose to 3.9% from a 49-year low of 3.7% as the percentage of working-age Americans in the labor force climbed to a five-year high.
“The far bigger than expected 312,000 jump in non-farm payrolls in December would seem to make a mockery of market fears of an impending recession. Admittedly, employment is a coincident indicator, whereas the ISM manufacturing index, which we learned yesterday fell sharply in December, is a leading indicator,” said Paul Ashworth, chief U.S. economist at Capital Economics.
“But, even allowing for that distinction, this employment report suggests the U.S. economy still has considerable forward momentum,” he said.
The euro EURUSD, +0.0439% changed hands at $1.1371, down from $1.1395 late Thursday. On Thursday, the Japanese yen soared in volatile and thin trade in early Asia-Pacific hours following Apple’s rare sales forecast cut. The dollar USDJPY, +0.74% rose to 108.29 yen, up from 107.66 late Thursday.
The British pound GBPUSD, +0.7599% trimmed an earlier rise to change hands at $1.2641 versus $1.2634 late Thursday.
China’s Commerce Ministry confirmed that a delegation of U.S. officials will travel to Beijing for a new round of trade talks on Monday and Tuesday, according to news reports.
Sentiment also got a boost after China’s central bank on Friday cut the ratio of cash that banks must hold as reserves by 100 basis points, or 1%, according to news reports — a move that has been seen as a means to help reduce the risk of a sharper slowdown in the world’s second-largest economy.
The dollar weakened Thursday as a sharp selloff on Wall Street following a warning from Apple Inc. AAPL, +4.27% and downbeat manufacturing survey data from China, the eurozone and the U.S. Global stocks were buoyed Friday, with U.S. stock-index futures pointing to a positive start for Wall Street.
